title: The Big Boss’s Little Wife
author: Lan Ya Lan
synopsis:
My cousin is a firm believer in remaining single. To get some peace and quiet, she begged Ling Ting to go on a blind date for her. Ling Ting went; although she thought the date was handsome and gentlemanly, she didn't give it much thought.
But what’s up with this new boss, who has a friendly smile and took the initiative to greet her?
He’s her blind date!
Ji Zhengyao: "Little comrade, we meet again."
Ling Ting: "...Hello, Boss."

chapters.title: Let’s Break Up
chapters.content:
In the sweltering heat of August, the weather made people feel irritable and restless.

After days of high temperatures, the old-fashioned fan in the snack shop creaked and rattled, looking like it might give up at any moment.

"Ling Ting, you know, it’s not easy for my family to save up for a down payment. My mom’s concerns are understandable, so how about..."

"How about we sign a prenuptial agreement?"

Qin Nan hung his head, his face flushed with embarrassment, his voice growing quieter and quieter.

Ling Ting gave a bitter smile. Looking at the boyfriend she had been with for two years, the disappointment in her heart had piled up like a mountain.

She and Qin Nan were university alumni, and their relationship had always been good.

Although he was usually a bit stingy—rarely buying her gifts and always taking her to street food stalls—Ling Ting had never minded.

But ever since they started talking about marriage, his penny-pinching had become increasingly obvious, and constantly crying poor had become the norm.

Ling Ting’s parents had died in an accident when she was fourteen, and she had always longed for a home of her own.

To avoid making things difficult for the Qin family, she hadn't asked for a bride price, only requesting that they prepare the marital home.

Yet even then, Qin Nan’s mother was unsatisfied. Not only did she demand that Ling Ting hand over her salary after marriage, but a few days ago, she had specifically called to hint, in a roundabout way, that there wasn't enough money for renovations.

Ling Ting had just passed the civil service exam last year and didn't have much savings, but thinking that she and Qin Nan would be living in the house later, she gritted her teeth and agreed to contribute thirty thousand yuan.

But it had only been a few days, and now there was another mess.

Sign a prenuptial agreement?

For a house with a down payment of over a hundred thousand, was that really necessary?

"Qin Nan, isn't your family going a bit too far?"

Ling Ting’s cheeks turned pale, her pleasant voice filled with grievance.

"Ling Ting... I'm sorry, but my mom..."

"It’s your mom again!"

Ling Ting sighed helplessly, her beautiful almond-shaped eyes brimming with mist. "Qin Nan, why is it always your mom this, your mom that? Don't you have a mind of your own?"

The reason she had been with Qin Nan was because of his steady personality, his ambition, and his drive.

But recently, Ling Ting had realized he had changed.

He had become irresponsible and lacked a sense of self; he was even willing to wrong her just to please his mother.

"Ling Ting, listen to yourself. What’s wrong with me mentioning my mom?"

Qin Nan was annoyed by Ling Ting’s words and retorted immediately.

But he didn't know that this sentence was like a sharp blade, stabbing fiercely into Ling Ting’s heart.

Ling Ting had grown up without a mother; he was deliberately picking at her softest spot.

"Qin Nan, let’s break up."

Ling Ting was utterly disappointed. Her lips trembled slightly as she stood up and walked out of the snack shop.

This relationship had reached its end; there was truly no way to continue.

"Ling Ting, how can you be like this? Are you only marrying me so you can divorce me later and take half the house?"

Qin Nan hadn't expected Ling Ting to suggest a breakup. Unable to save face, he chased her to the entrance and roared at her slender back.

Ling Ting paused but didn't look back. The scorching sun made her vision go black, and her steps were unsteady; she was nearly hit by a passing vehicle.

"I'm sorry."

She hurriedly apologized to the driver and quickened her pace, rushing across the road in one breath.

She hopped onto the first bus that came along, stumbled to the back row, and fished a candy from her bag to pop into her mouth. Only after a long while did her vision gradually clear.

Looking out at the bustling traffic with a sense of loss, Ling Ting pursed her lips. A tidal wave of sadness nearly swallowed her whole.

The little home she had looked forward to with all her heart had, after all, been nothing more than a pipe dream.

After riding the bus in a large loop, Ling Ting returned to her aunt’s house in the evening, her eyes swollen from crying.

"Lin Wei, the person Auntie Huang introduced to you this time is not only handsome but also comes from a good family. Just consider it."

As soon as she opened the door, Ling Ting heard her aunt’s delighted voice.

"Mom, how many times do I have to tell you? I don't want to get married."

Lin Wei was wearing a cool camisole, her curly hair tied loosely behind her head, lounging on the sofa while leisurely eating snacks.

"What do you mean you don't want to get married? Do you want to be an old maid for the rest of your life?"

Tian Rong frowned, disapproving of her daughter’s words.

"So what if I’m an old maid? I’m happy to be one."

Lin Wei popped a potato chip into her mouth, unbothered.

"You..."

Tian Rong took a deep breath and softened her tone. "Can you just give me some peace of mind for once?"

"If you stopped meddling in everything, you’d have peace of mind naturally."

Lin Wei raised an eyebrow and glanced sideways at Ling Ting, who was standing at the door like a wooden statue.

*Sigh...* Here we go again.

Ling Ting silently put her keys in her bag and lowered her head to change into slippers, not daring to chime in for fear of getting caught in the crossfire.

Her cousin was twenty-nine this year. She was very beautiful, had a great figure, and a good job; the only thing she lacked was a boyfriend.

Her aunt, seeing that her peers’ grandchildren were already old enough to run errands, was anxious and often asked old friends to introduce men to her cousin.

But her cousin wouldn't have it, and the two of them bickering was a common occurrence.

"Lin Wei, are you trying to be the death of me?"

Tian Rong suddenly exploded, giving Ling Ting a start.

"Auntie, please calm down. Talk to my cousin nicely."

Ling Ting sensed things were going south and hurried over.

"She doesn't understand reason; talking to her is a waste of breath."

Tian Rong wiped away non-existent tears from her face and grabbed Ling Ting to vent her grievances. "Ling Ting, tell me, is it easy for me? I’ve got one foot in the grave, and I still can't even hold a grandchild."

"Auntie, you will, you definitely will."

Ling Ting held her aunt’s hand, coaxing her with a soft voice.

"If you want one so bad, have one yourself. Don't you dare put that on me."

Lin Wei snorted and curled her lip. "I’m not as shortsighted as you."

Ling Ting understood what her cousin meant, and thinking of the Qin family’s behavior, the corners of her eyes turned red again.

"I’ve raised this daughter for nothing. I’m cutting ties with you!"

Hearing her aunt make such a harsh threat, Ling Ting sniffled and held back her tears. "Cousin, just go and meet him. Maybe you’ll be a good match."

"What do you know! I’m not going."

Lin Wei rolled her eyes dramatically and flopped back onto the sofa, looking like a dead pig that wasn't afraid of boiling water.

"Fine, you’re not going, right?"

Tian Rong pointed at Lin Wei and asked threateningly.

"Not going."

Lin Wei answered flatly, not even sparing her mother a glance.

"Good!"

Tian Rong nodded indignantly and turned to rush into the bedroom.

"Since you think I meddle too much, then I’m leaving!"

"Auntie, where are you going?"

Ling Ting followed her in, seeing her aunt packing clothes, and shouted toward the living room, "Cousin!"

"I’ll go wherever I end up; it’s better than being angered to death by her."

Tian Rong shoved clothes into her bag haphazardly, feeling utterly disappointed.

"Auntie, please don't say things you don't mean."

Ling Ting snatched the clothes from her hands, hoping her cousin would hurry up and give in.

"Ling Ting, don't stop me. I’m leaving right now, and I’m never coming back!"

Tian Rong wailed, shouting at the top of her lungs.

"Alright, enough! I’ll go, I’ll go, is that good enough for you!"

Lin Wei knew her mother was doing this on purpose, but to end the farce as quickly as possible, she had no choice but to agree.

"Are you serious?"

Tian Rong stopped what she was doing and asked, full of anticipation.

"Believe it or not."

Lin Wei returned to her room, slamming the door so hard it shook the house.

chapters.title: Blind Date on Behalf of My Cousin
chapters.content:
Tian Rong, who had been planning to put on a performance for a while longer, beamed with joy the moment her daughter finally relented.

"Good, good, good. As long as you agree, I’m off to play mahjong."

She tossed the half-packed clothes to Ling Ting, patted her on the shoulder, and left in high spirits.

Ling Ting: "..."

Only her aunt could pull off such a seamless performance.

She truly lived up to her reputation as a veteran actress from the drama troupe.

"Ling Ting, what’s wrong?"

Lin Wei was a lawyer with a sharp eye. Hearing the door close, she walked out of her room.

She had noticed earlier that Ling Ting’s expression was off and her eyes were swollen like walnuts.

"Nothing."

Ling Ting hadn't expected to be found out so quickly. Feeling guilty, she turned her face away and scrambled to tidy up the clothes on the bed.

"Tell me, now."

Lin Wei had an impatient personality; she didn't give Ling Ting any chance to evade her and stepped to the side to block her path.

"I..."

Ling Ting didn't know how to start.

"Oh, spit it out."

Lin Wei frowned impatiently and pulled the clothes out of Ling Ting's hands, tossing them aside.

"Cousin, I broke up with Qin Nan."

Ling Ting didn't look up, but her trembling voice betrayed her sadness.

"What?"

Lin Wei was shocked. "Did he bully you?"

Naturally protective of her own, Lin Wei’s voice rose sharply.

"No, I just suddenly saw things clearly."

Ling Ting let out a slow breath and sat weakly on the edge of the bed.

Because she lacked a sense of security, she had always believed that as long as she got married, her heart would finally be at peace.

But the events of this past period had taught her that she was too naive.

Marriage wasn't necessarily a harbor; it could be a source of trouble.

"You really saw things clearly?"

Lin Wei sat down beside Ling Ting. Without waiting for an answer, she said, "It’s better that you broke up. Besides, that Qin Nan’s circumstances are average, and his character isn't much better."

Lin Wei had long seen that the Qin family was a handful, but since her cousin liked him, she hadn't interfered too much.

Now that Ling Ting had come to her senses on her own, it was exactly what she wanted.

"Cousin, you're going on a blind date tomorrow, right?"

Ling Ting didn't want to talk about her own miserable affairs, so she wiped the corners of her eyes and changed the subject.

"Listen to me, I'm not going."

Lin Wei waved her hand; what she had said earlier was just to fool her mother.

"Then..."

Ling Ting was worried her aunt would make a scene when she found out tomorrow.

Lin Wei had naturally anticipated what Ling Ting was thinking.

She didn't know what had gotten into her mother over the past year; she was obsessed with having a grandchild and was truly driving her crazy.

But after all, her mother was older and had undergone major surgery last year, so Lin Wei felt helpless.

"Huh?"

Lin Wei’s eyes lit up, and she looked at Ling Ting with a pleasant surprise.

"Since you’ve broken up with Qin Nan anyway, why don't you go on the blind date for me?"

"What?"

Ling Ting hadn't expected her cousin to have such an idea and shook her head immediately. "No way..."

"What do you mean 'no way'?"

Lin Wei knitted her brows. "Do you still want to be with Qin Nan?"

"No."

Ling Ting denied it; there was no possibility for her and Qin Nan anymore.

"Then that settles it!"

Lin Wei was meticulous in her actions. After confirming repeatedly that Ling Ting really didn't want to get married anymore, she picked up her phone and called Qin Nan’s mother.

"Our Ling Ting has had a sudden awakening and doesn't want to be bullied by you anymore. The engagement is off."

With that, she hung up the phone without waiting for Qin Nan’s mother to blather on.

"Now you two have officially broken up, and as your family, I agree. Go on the blind date."

Seeing that Ling Ting still wanted to refuse, Lin Wei went to her room, found a new set of cosmetics she had just bought, and tossed them to her. "Do me a favor, good cousin."

After saying that, she scurried away.

Ling Ting: "..."

Her cousin had run off, and she had accepted the gift; it wouldn't be right not to go.

After agonizing over it all night, Ling Ting finally decided to go on the blind date for her cousin.

It was just a formality anyway; she would go and come right back.

It would fool her aunt, or else the mother and daughter would just end up arguing.

Because she hadn't slept well, Ling Ting’s state was poor the next day, but after applying some lipstick, her complexion improved.

Ling Ting had a sweet appearance and fair skin. To match the meeting location, she specifically chose a dress.

The dress was a gift from her cousin after she passed the civil service exam; it had elbow-length sleeves and a cinched waist, which looked particularly flattering.

After turning around in front of the mirror and finding nothing wrong, she added the calling Qin Nan to her blacklist and left for the city center.

When she arrived at the designated cafe, her date hadn't arrived yet. Ling Ting found a random seat and asked the waiter for a glass of water.

She had been afraid of bitterness since she was a child and rarely drank coffee.

She picked up the glass, took a small sip, and looked around, feeling a little nervous.

She had grown up and never been on a blind date before.

"Are you Miss Lin?"

A deep, magnetic voice sounded. Ling Ting looked up and was stunned by the man’s appearance.

The man had an extraordinary temperament and a gentle gaze. With his rimless glasses, he gave off a refreshing, spring-like feeling.

Her aunt was right; the blind date was indeed very handsome.

"Hello, my name is Ling... Lin Wei."

Ling Ting awkwardly tugged at the corner of her mouth and introduced herself, looking somewhat restrained.

The blind date scenes on TV seemed to always start with self-introductions.

Ji Zhengyao was very busy and had intended to just say hello and leave. But when he saw the restrained girl in front of him, with her small face tilted up and red, swollen eyes like a wounded little rabbit, he froze in place.

He stood there like a statue. Time seemed to stop at that moment, and long-sealed memories in his mind flashed by like a movie.

"Hello?"

Seeing that her date wasn't moving, Ling Ting felt a bit puzzled. She tilted her head and called out to him softly.

"Ji Zhengyao."

Awakened by the pleasant voice, Ji Zhengyao suppressed the agitation in his heart, stated his name, and pulled out a chair to sit down.

"The matchmaker said you are twenty-nine?"

Ji Zhengyao stared at the face that overlapped with his memories, his hands unconsciously clasping together.

"Ah?"

Ling Ting wasn't good at lying, but for her cousin, she went all in.

"Yes, I'm twenty-nine."

In reality, she was only twenty-five by lunar age, and her birthday was on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month.

Ji Zhengyao nodded and called the waiter to order a black coffee.

He didn't speak during this time, but his gaze remained fixed on Ling Ting’s face.

Ling Ting had only just graduated, and being stared at by those deep, dark eyes made her feel instantly unnatural.

She picked up her water glass and gulped down two large mouthfuls.

"Miss Lin, have we met somewhere before?"

Ji Zhengyao was amused by Ling Ting’s cute manner. He stirred his coffee gently and asked, full of anticipation.

"I don't think so?"

Ling Ting glanced secretly at the time on her phone and answered distractedly.

"Clack."

The spoon in his hand hit the rim of the cup. Ji Zhengyao’s brows twitched slightly, but he returned to normal after a moment.

"Then I must have remembered wrong."

His voice carried a faint hint of disappointment.

Ling Ting didn't notice anything wrong with Ji Zhengyao. Seeing that the time was about right, she said, "Mr. Ji, I have something to attend to, so I should be going."

Her cousin had said that if she sat for five minutes, it would be enough—polite and proper.

"You're leaving already?"

chapters.title: Adding Contact Information
chapters.content:
A strange glimmer flickered in Ji Zhengyao’s long, narrow eyes, and his voice tightened. "Not staying for a while longer?"

"No, I really have things to do."

Ling Ting smiled and stood up.

Seeing that she was determined to leave, Ji Zhengyao pondered for a moment. "I’ll drop you off."

"That’s not necessary, is it?"

Ling Ting racked her brain, trying to find a reason to refuse.

"It’s fine."

Ji Zhengyao didn't give Ling Ting a chance to decline. After paying the bill, he walked toward the exit of the coffee shop first.

Ling Ting had no choice but to follow him.

Ji Zhengyao was not only handsome but also had an excellent build; Ling Ting estimated he was at least 1.8 meters tall.

His posture was upright, one hand tucked into the pocket of his well-tailored suit trousers. He walked with a calm and composed air, his movements particularly graceful.

Her cousin was beautiful and confident; the two of them would certainly make a perfect match.

"Ouch!"

Lost in her own thoughts, she didn't notice that the person in front had stopped, and Ling Ting bumped straight into Ji Zhengyao.

A faint, woody, cool scent drifted into her nose.

"I forgot, we haven't added each other's contact information yet."

A faint smile hung on the corners of Ji Zhengyao’s mouth, his eyes filled with amusement as he took out his phone and gave it a little shake.

Uh...

Ling Ting didn't want to add him, but since she had to play the part to the end, she reluctantly scanned his QR code while he waited.

"Ting?"

Ji Zhengyao looked at Ling Ting’s WeChat name, his brows twitching as he murmured it under his breath.

"Mr. Ji, my friend is nearby, so there's no need to trouble you with a ride."

Ling Ting pointed into the distance, making a move to leave.

"Ms. Lin!"

Ji Zhengyao called out to stop her.

"When will you be free? I’d like to treat you to a meal."

Ji Zhengyao locked eyes with Ling Ting’s dark, grape-like pupils, hoping for an opportunity as early as tomorrow.

"I’m very busy these next two days, I’m sorry."

Ling Ting refused without a second thought. Once she finished speaking, she turned and ran, as if afraid that Ji Zhengyao might pester her.

"You..."

Watching Ling Ting’s rapidly disappearing back, the face that had been pleasant just a moment ago instantly darkened.

Was he really that terrifying?

"Uncle, all done?"

Ji Yunxiao strolled out from a corner with a head of bleached hair, the charms on his jeans jingling; he didn't look like a serious person at all.

"Why are you here?"

Ji Zhengyao glanced at the nephew who had tricked him by faking an injury, his voice cold.

"Me?"

Ji Yunxiao awkwardly scratched his nose with one finger, smiling ingratiatingly. "Uncle, you have to understand me."

With that, he draped an arm over Ji Zhengyao’s shoulder like they were best buddies.

"Uncle, don't be mad. I was just backed into a corner by my mom."

The person supposed to be on the blind date today was actually him. Knowing his uncle was coming to the area for business, he had drafted him as a temporary substitute.

Of course, he had told a little lie.

"So you really don't want to go on a blind date?"

Ji Zhengyao didn't want to bicker with his nephew; he brushed his hand off and walked toward his car.

"I’m only twenty-eight, why would I go on a blind date?"

"You’re already thirty-one, and you’re not in any rush either, are you?"

Ji Yunxiao followed behind Ji Zhengyao, muttering to himself.

The family was really something—they didn't dare pressure his uncle about marriage, so they insisted on forcing him.

They really knew how to pick on the soft targets.

"Stop following me."

Ji Zhengyao had things on his mind and didn't want to listen to Ji Yunxiao’s nonsense. He opened the car door and got in.

"Uncle, it’s been so long since we last saw each other. I heard you got a promotion—aren't we going to celebrate?"

Ji Yunxiao was naturally fond of excitement. His uncle had been exceptionally promoted to the position of bureau chief at only thirty-one; it was a cause for celebration.

"No need."

Ji Zhengyao waved his hand, signaling for Ji Yunxiao to step back, and the car sped off with a press of the accelerator.

Watching the car disappear, Ji Yunxiao shook his head. While feeling sorry for his uncle, who was as busy as a spinning top every day, he felt relieved that he hadn't gone into politics.

Recalling his wise decision to throw a tantrum to avoid that path, Ji Yunxiao shoved his hands into his pockets and whistled as he walked away.

There was a racing meet tonight, and he had to get there early to prepare.

Ling Ting had no idea that it wasn't supposed to be Ji Zhengyao on the blind date with her cousin. It took her a long time to find the bus stop.

"Ling Ting, what is the meaning of this?"

After changing buses twice, she had finally reached the entrance of her apartment building. Just as she was about to breathe a sigh of relief, her path was blocked by a slender figure.

Qin Nan’s face was flushed red, and the hair on his forehead was damp with sweat, showing he had been waiting for a long time.

"I thought I made my meaning clear yesterday."

Ling Ting gripped her backpack straps, trying to suppress the sense of grievance in her heart, her expression indifferent.

"Ling Ting, we’re about to get married. Can you stop acting out?"

In Qin Nan’s eyes, Ling Ting was just throwing a temper tantrum.

Otherwise, why would she have blocked him?

"Qin Nan, I am not acting out."

Ling Ting pulled the corners of her mouth into a bitter smile and said hoarsely, "Qin Nan, we can’t go on like this."

The ideal marriage in her heart was one based on discussion, mutual understanding, and mutual tolerance.

Qin Nan was incapable of that.

He and his mother were consumed by calculations.

"Ling Ting, can you be a bit more sensible? My mother is sick."

Qin Nan had assumed that if he came over and coaxed her a little, Ling Ting would have a change of heart.

Then he would take her home to sincerely apologize to his mother, and the matter would be resolved.

After all, Ling Ting was reasonable and very easy to coax.

But Ling Ting, who had always been easygoing, had suddenly changed, catching him off guard.

"If your mother is sick, take her to the hospital. Why are you coming to our building to shout?"

Lin Wei happened to be coming out to take out the trash and, hearing Qin Nan’s words, was immediately displeased.

"Cousin, that’s not how you put it. My mother is sick entirely because of..."

Qin Nan wanted to say "because of that phone call from you."

But after a moment’s thought, he changed his words: "Because she’s been worried and anxious about things between me and Ling Ting."

Qin Nan disliked Lin Wei the most because she always acted so high and mighty.

But she had a strong presence and a sharp tongue, so he had to be careful with his words.

After all, Lin Wei wasn't Ling Ting; she would turn against you in a heartbeat.

"Don't blame everything on Ling Ting."

Lin Wei walked over and stood in front of Ling Ting, crossing her arms like a mother hen protecting her chick.

"Ling Ting, can we talk alone?"

Qin Nan didn't want to argue with Lin Wei; he frowned and looked at Ling Ting behind her.

"I have nothing to say to you."

Ling Ting avoided Qin Nan’s expectant gaze and turned her face away.

"Ling Ting!"

At first, when Ling Ting suggested breaking up, Qin Nan thought she was just speaking in anger.

After all, when he thought back on it, he also felt his mother had gone too far.

But now, Ling Ting’s resolute attitude suddenly gave him a sense of crisis.

"Ling Ting, is it really because of the prenuptial agreement?"

"If it is, we can discuss it further."

Qin Nan thought that if Ling Ting really minded, they didn't have to sign the prenuptial agreement.

"What did you say?"

Because Ling Ting hadn't gone into detail, Lin Wei didn't know the real reason for their breakup.

Hearing now that his family had actually forced Ling Ting to sign a prenuptial agreement, she was furious.

"Is your family sick? You didn't pay a single cent in bride price, and you still want a prenuptial agreement? Are you bullying us because you think we have no one to stand up for us?"

Lin Wei had a fiery temper and exploded right then and there.

chapters.title: Mama’s Boy
chapters.content:
She grabbed Ling Ting’s hand, pointed at Qin Nan, and cursed, "This dog of a man is clearly a mama’s boy. Forget about you breaking up with him; even if you wanted to get back together, I wouldn't allow it!"

Having said that, Lin Wei still felt it wasn't enough and kicked Qin Nan right in the shin.

"Ouch!"

Qin Nan clutched his leg and glared at Lin Wei in anger.

Lin Wei wasn't afraid of him at all. She slammed the unit door shut and dragged Ling Ting back into the apartment.

"Something this big, why didn't you tell me sooner?"

"Do you even consider us family? Do you treat your cousin like a piece of furniture?"

Lin Wei stood with her hands on her hips, her delicate brows arched in anger. "You get bullied like this and don't even know to ask for help? Are you stupid?"

If she had known the Qin family was being so insulting, she wouldn't have made that phone call yesterday; she would have gone over there directly.

That old hag, actually daring to scheme against her cousin?

Signing a prenuptial agreement?

What does she think her family is?

"Cousin, I'm fine."

Seeing her cousin angry, Ling Ting quickly pulled her down to sit on the sofa.

"Didn't I break up with him?"

Ling Ting tugged at the corners of her lips, trying to force a smile that looked worse than crying. "As you would say, I cut my losses in time."

"Hmph, it's a good thing you ran fast."

Lin Wei, frustrated by her lack of backbone, reached out and poked Ling Ting on the forehead.

This cousin of hers used to be lively and cheerful as a child, jumping around like a little monkey.

But ever since her aunt and uncle passed away, her personality had changed.

She became quiet, a real wallflower.

Lin Wei originally wanted to scold her a bit more, but seeing her aggrieved expression, she couldn't bring herself to do it.

"Qin Nan is no good, Ling Ting. Whatever you do, don't look back."

Worried that Ling Ting lacked resolve and might get back together after a few sweet words from Qin Nan, Lin Wei gave her a rare, gentle warning.

"Cousin, I won't."

Ling Ting shook her head. "There’s no possibility for us anymore."

Her relationship with Qin Nan had reached its end the moment he mocked her for not having a mother.

"Hmm, good girl."

Lin Wei patted Ling Ting’s head, her heart aching for her.

Seeing that her cousin wasn't as angry anymore, Ling Ting finally let out a sigh of relief. After thinking for a moment, she brought up the blind date from earlier today.

"Cousin, that Mr. Ji is a man of talent and appearance, and he’s exceptionally polite. You..."

"Alright, alright. Even if he looked like a blooming flower, I wouldn't care."

Lin Wei waved her hand dismissively, not taking it seriously at all.

She didn't want to get married, at least not right now.

"Alright then."

Seeing her cousin’s firm attitude, Ling Ting didn't try to persuade her further. She made an excuse about being tired and went back to her room.

Having been with Qin Nan for two years, Ling Ting was actually heartbroken, even though she pretended to be indifferent on the surface.

In her room, Ling Ting hid under the covers and cried secretly, not daring to let her cousin hear.

Meanwhile, Ji Zhengyao returned to the old family mansion after finishing his business and locked himself in the study.

He stood before the floor-to-ceiling window with a nearly burnt-out cigarette between his fingers. Without his glasses to hide them, his eyes were like a raging sea.

Ten years. He never thought he would see her again.

Recalling what happened back then, Ji Zhengyao gently pressed his hand against his pounding heart and closed his eyes slightly.

The clock ticked away, each beat feeling like it was striking his heart, and the gears of fate were slowly realigning.

The little girl has grown up...

He wanted to make her his own!

"Uncle, what are you doing?"

Ji Yunxiao pushed the door open and threw himself onto the sofa, acting boisterous and completely at home.

"How did you end up like this in such a short time?"

Ji Zhengyao glanced at the bandage on Ji Yunxiao’s head, put his glasses back on, and asked with a cold face.

"It’s nothing, just a small injury."

Ji Yunxiao grinned carelessly, hissed in pain, and said, "A tire blew out just as I was starting."

"You're not a kid anymore. Stop playing around with that stuff."

Ji Zhengyao stubbed out his cigarette, warned Ji Yunxiao, and walked toward the door.

Racing was too dangerous; he would have to mention it to his sister-in-law when he had a chance.

"Uncle, wait for me!"

Ji Yunxiao had wanted to get his uncle to cover for him, so seeing him leave, he immediately chased after him.

"Solve your own problems. I’m busy."

Ji Zhengyao knew exactly what his nephew was up to, but he had business with the old man today and didn't want to deal with him.

"Uncle!"

Seeing his uncle enter his grandfather’s study, Ji Yunxiao looked desperate, his voice sounding miserable and desolate.

"Your uncle has serious business. Can you stop bothering him?"

Wen Yazhi came out of the kitchen with a plate of fruit. Seeing her son tagging along behind his uncle like a puppy, she said irritably.

"Mom, I have things to do. I won't be eating dinner."

Ji Yunxiao shrank his neck and tried to hide the injury on his head with his hand, but just as he was about to leave, his mother called out to him.

"Yunxiao, what happened to your head?"

Wen Yazhi walked up to her son, looked at his head, and asked with concern.

"It's nothing. I was running an errand for Uncle and bumped it by accident."

Ji Yunxiao dodged his mother’s hand and immediately used his uncle as a shield.

"Really?"

Wen Yazhi was a bit skeptical.

Her brother-in-law was always measured in his actions; how could he let her son get hurt?

"Oh Mom, if you don't believe me, just ask Uncle later."

Ji Yunxiao was certain that if his mother asked, his uncle would help him cover it up.

They had an unspoken understanding since childhood; they both knew how it worked.

"Sigh, be more careful in the future."

Seeing that her son didn't seem to be lying, Wen Yazhi nodded and pulled him down to sit.

"Be careful when you shower. Don't get it wet."

The boy wasn't much younger than his uncle, but the difference in their maturity was like night and day.

"Got it."

With the alarm cleared, Ji Yunxiao secretly breathed a sigh of relief.

"Yunxiao, how did the blind date go today?"

Ji Yunxiao had thought that once this hurdle was passed, he could wait for dinner in peace. But before he could be happy for long, his mother brought up the blind date.

"It... it was okay."

Ji Yunxiao grunted, forced to lie.

"Is the girl very pretty?"

Wen Yazhi was very surprised that her son didn't belittle the other person, so she smiled and continued to ask.

Her son had a sharp tongue; being able to say it was "okay" was already a very high compliment.

"She's alright."

Ji Yunxiao was getting anxious, glancing toward his grandfather’s study every few seconds, thinking to himself, *Uncle, why aren't you coming out yet?*

*I'm waiting for you to save me.*

"Did you exchange contact information? Can you try getting to know each other?"

Wen Yazhi didn't notice the guilt on her son's face and kept asking on her own.

"We added each other, we added each other. Oh Mom, can you give us some private space?"

Worried that he would slip up if they kept talking, Ji Yunxiao pretended to be impatient.

Surprisingly, this tactic worked quite well on Wen Yazhi.

"Alright, alright. I won't interfere in you young people's business. Just get along well."

It was rare for her son to show interest in a girl; she couldn't let him ruin it.

Yunxiao was twenty-eight. Wen Yazhi had considered finding him a match from a family of equal status.

But the young ladies in their social circle were all too arrogant, and her son had no real skills other than playing around. After much deliberation, she decided to find him someone ordinary.

She heard the girl was a lawyer, very capable, and pretty too.

Wen Yazhi had a small selfish motive: she hoped her future daughter-in-law would be a bit feisty so she could keep her good-for-nothing son in check.

She didn't have many requirements; as long as her son didn't cause trouble for the family, that was enough.

chapters.title: The Division Chief’s Assignment
chapters.content:
Tian Rong was another person who, like Wen Yazhi, possessed a mother’s heart and hoped this blind date would be a success.

As soon as she returned from playing mahjong, she couldn’t wait to press Lin Wei for details.

Lin Wei had originally intended to say she wasn’t interested, as that had been her plan from the start. But since her cousin had just gone through a breakup, Lin Wei didn’t want to worry her mother, so she gritted her teeth and lied, saying she would try getting to know him.

Tian Rong knew Lin Wei’s personality well and, fearing she might be pulling a fast one, specifically called Aunt Huang. Once she received confirmation, she was completely relieved.

Overjoyed, Tian Rong cooked dinner herself, whipping up several dishes in one go.

Seeing her aunt in such high spirits, Ling Ting exchanged a look with her cousin and slipped away as soon as she finished eating. She didn’t know what the situation was like on the man’s side, and she was afraid that if the truth came out, her aunt would give her a piece of her mind...

After her parents passed away, Ling Ting had always lived at her aunt’s house. Although she attended university in another city, she would return during winter and summer breaks. However, because her workplace was too far away and the daily commute was inconvenient, she had no choice but to rent a place of her own.

The apartment was very small, just a single room and a living room, but its only advantage was that it was close to her office—it only took ten minutes to get to work.

Having been away for two days, the potted flowers on the windowsill had wilted a bit. Setting down her bag, Ling Ting hurriedly watered them. Looking at the little flowers she had carefully nurtured, she saw two new buds, and her terrible mood finally improved a little.

She trimmed the leaves, talked to the plants about the grievances she had suffered over the past two days, and before she knew it, she began to feel sleepy.

Ling Ting’s sleep was very restless; her dreams were filled with the little moments she had shared with Qin Nan over the past two years. She could clearly feel Qin Nan’s tenderness, yet she could also feel the pain of having been schemed against.

"Ring, ring, ring."

The phone suddenly rang, startling Ling Ting. She felt a moment of confusion the instant she opened her eyes.

"Hello?"

Because she was stressed, Ling Ting’s voice was hoarse and weak.

"Xiao Ling, the new bureau chief is taking office tomorrow. You need to prepare immediately."

The call was from Division Chief Huang at her office. His voice was urgent and tense, giving the illusion that some great disaster was imminent.

"Chief, prepare what?"

Ling Ting slowly sat up, her mind still in a fog. The new bureau chief was coming—what did that have to do with a low-level employee like her?

"The welcome speech, of course." Division Chief Huang said earnestly, "Xiao Ling, it’s time for you to show what you can do."

Ling Ting was puzzled. "Chief, hasn't Sister Wang always written the welcome speeches in the past?" Why was it her turn this time?

"Just write it if I tell you to. Why so much nonsense?"

Division Chief Huang didn't offer any further explanation; he just told Ling Ting to get it ready quickly and then hung up the phone decisively.

Listening to the dial tone, Ling Ting glanced at the wall clock and pouted. It was eleven o'clock at night—was the Division Chief not planning on letting her sleep?

Although she was very reluctant, she didn't have the guts to refuse. She opened her laptop and resignedly began to write the welcome speech. After checking past records, it took her over two hours to finally complete the task assigned by Division Chief Huang.

Because she went to bed late and had been dreaming all night, Ling Ting woke up a bit late the next day and didn't arrive at the office until after eight.

"Oh my, Xiao Ling, why are you only just getting here?"

As soon as Ling Ting walked into the office, Division Chief Huang rushed in, his head with its few remaining hairs glistening.

"Chief, I’m not late." Ling Ting specifically checked the time; it was only 8:15.

"Fine, fine. Where is the welcome speech?" Division Chief Huang didn't have time to argue about lateness and held out his hand to her.

"Oh." Ling Ting realized that Division Chief Huang hadn't come to scold her for being late, so she quickly handed over the welcome speech she had already printed.

*Creak.*

Seeing the welcome speech in her hand, Sister Wang’s expression darkened instantly, and she shoved her chair back forcefully. The chair legs scraped against the floor, making a harsh sound that made Ling Ting shrink her shoulders in fright.

"The new bureau chief will be here shortly. You all need to prepare well and go downstairs to wait in advance." Division Chief Huang glanced at Sister Wang, frowned imperceptibly, and turned to leave. He was overwhelmed and had no time to deal with her.

"Hmph!" Sister Wang curled her lip and sat back down at her desk.

"Ling Ting, when did the Chief tell you to write the welcome speech?" Sister Wang, sporting a cheap perm, crossed her arms and looked at Ling Ting, looking like she was ready to hold her accountable. She had known about the new bureau chief’s arrival for a long time, but she didn't know when that old man, Division Chief Huang, had handed the task of writing the speech to Ling Ting.

"Last night," Ling Ting added, "at eleven o'clock."

Seeing Sister Wang’s face grow increasingly ugly, Ling Ting awkwardly pursed her lips and sat quietly at her desk.

How should one describe Sister Wang? When she was in a good mood, she was like a caring older sister, laughing and chatting with colleagues. When she was unhappy, she wore a long face, as if everyone owed her money.

Ling Ting was certain that if this welcome speech had been assigned to her, she would have complained endlessly. But now that it had been given to someone else, she was unhappy about that too. Ling Ting didn't know what her problem was, but since they shared an office and she was the newcomer, it wasn't good to keep the tension going.

"Sister Wang, what time is the new bureau chief coming?" Ling Ting asked, trying to make small talk in a soft voice.

"Who knows." Sister Wang was busy filing her nails; it took a long time before she replied.

Sensing that Sister Wang didn't really want to talk to her, Ling Ting nodded and didn't press further. Being overly eager wasn't worth it; out of respect, initiating conversation once was enough.

"It's already noon. Is he still coming or not?" Sister Wang had been angry all morning, but her expression finally softened a bit. She checked the time and started to get anxious. She had a severe stomach condition and had always been very regular with her meal times.

"Should we order takeout?" Xiao Liu, who worked in the same office, returned from outside and smiled at the two of them. He had noticed that other offices seemed to be ordering takeout as well.

"Let's order then. I really can't take it anymore." Sister Wang glanced downstairs again and agreed wholeheartedly.

Ling Ting went with the flow. "Takeout is fine." Although she wasn't particularly hungry, she would follow the majority.

Seeing that they all agreed, Xiao Liu took out his phone. But before he could even open the app, colleagues from the neighboring office swarmed toward the stairs.

"Oh, the new bureau chief is coming!" Sister Wang leaned against the window to look, and seeing that many colleagues had already gathered downstairs, she hurriedly shouted at Ling Ting and Xiao Liu.

Hearing that the leader was arriving, Ling Ting didn't dare to delay and followed everyone downstairs. Once downstairs, Ling Ting hid behind her colleagues, trying to stand in an inconspicuous spot. She had always been like this; she was just there to make up the numbers, so there was no need to push to the front.

"I wonder what the new bureau chief's background is." Sister Wang whispered to a woman from the department next door.

"I heard he's very impressive. He was already making waves at his old unit at such a young age. You can tell just by how much importance Division Chief Huang is placing on this." The woman tilted her chin. Ling Ting followed her gaze and noticed that Division Chief Huang seemed very nervous, pacing back and forth.

Having been at the unit for so long, Ling Ting had heard some rumors. Division Chief Huang had someone backing him, someone who was supposedly a very high-ranking official. But his behavior today was strange—he looked for all the world like a primary school student on his first day of class.

Could the new bureau chief really be so formidable that he had reached a level that even made Division Chief Huang wary?

While Ling Ting was lost in thought, after waiting for about five minutes, a black sedan slowly drove in.

chapters.title: Little Ling, is it?
chapters.content:
The division chief rushed over at lightning speed to open the car door for the new bureau chief, his face full of fawning, looking every bit the sycophant.

Ling Ting blinked, genuinely admiring Division Chief Huang’s thick skin.

The bureau chief’s position had been vacant for some time, and Division Chief Huang had practically been walking around the office like he owned the place; everyone thought he had the position in the bag.

Now that the new bureau chief had arrived, it was unexpected to see him adjust his attitude so quickly.

No wonder he was the one in power; you really had to hand it to him.

Ling Ting had a good temperament and was usually quiet. She stood in the last row of the crowd, and even though her inner monologue was incredibly lively, she didn't show it on her face, so no one noticed.

But just as she was enjoying her internal rant, she suddenly felt her scalp tingle. She looked up and locked eyes with a playful gaze.

It was her blind date!

No, it was her cousin’s blind date?!

Ling Ting’s beautiful almond eyes widened abruptly, her lips slightly parted, as if she couldn't comprehend the scene before her.

Oh my god!

Her aunt only said the man had good credentials; she hadn't expected them to be this good.

The new bureau chief?

Ling Ting quickly dodged that gaze, shrinking her neck and hiding behind Sister Wang.

Oh no, she wondered if he had recognized her?

Ling Ting’s small, nervous face turned pale. She looked left and right, desperately wanting to slip back to the office while no one was paying attention.

But before she could put that into action, a pair of polished black leather shoes appeared before her eyes.

“Miss Lin?”

Ji Zhengyao looked at the little girl who was wishing she could vanish into thin air, his eyes full of smiles. He wore an amiable expression that was every bit the leader.

“Bureau Chief Ji, this is Little Ling, Ling Ting.”

Hearing Ji Zhengyao get Ling Ting’s surname wrong, Division Chief Huang hurriedly stepped forward to help introduce her.

“Ling Ting?”

Ji Zhengyao raised an eyebrow with interest, the smile in his eyes carrying a deep meaning.

With her lie exposed, Ling Ting’s small face turned from white to red. Her hands unconsciously tightened on the hem of her shirt, and she was so embarrassed she wished she could crawl into a crack in the floor.

“How old are you?”

Ji Zhengyao stared at the top of Ling Ting’s head, the smile at the corners of his mouth never fading.

“Twenty...”

“Twenty-four!”

Seeing that Ling Ting was struggling to speak, Division Chief Huang chimed in to answer for her.

“Oh~”

Ji Zhengyao nodded, looking as if he understood everything.

“This young comrade is quite interesting.”

After saying this remark, which carried a hidden meaning, Ji Zhengyao didn't linger and followed Division Chief Huang toward the conference room.

The others followed in a rush.

Seeing that Ji Zhengyao had left, Ling Ting finally let out the breath she had been holding.

“Are you alright?”

Seeing that Ling Ting looked a bit off, Little Liu asked with concern.

“I’m fine.”

Ling Ting shook her head.

“If you’re fine, let’s go.”

Little Liu looked Ling Ting up and down, and seeing that she really seemed okay, followed the main group.

Ling Ting took a deep breath, hesitated on the spot for a long time, and then slowly shuffled toward the conference room.

She was truly shuffling, because by the time she reached the conference room, Division Chief Huang was already halfway through his welcome speech.

Don't let Division Chief Huang’s unremarkable, short, and stout appearance fool you; he had a truly powerful voice.

His voice was so loud that even without a microphone, everyone in the conference room could hear him clearly.

Ling Ting snuck a glance at Ji Zhengyao, who was sitting there smiling as if he were listening intently. She hunched her shoulders and slouched, walking to the last row to sit down, wishing she could embed herself into the wall.

She didn't dare look up because it was just too awkward.

Going on a blind date for her cousin and ending up with her own direct superior—who would believe that if she told them?

Just as Ling Ting was debating whether to slip away early and keep her distance from Ji Zhengyao, thunderous applause erupted in the conference room.

“Thank you.”

Ji Zhengyao nodded at Division Chief Huang and said, “Comrades, I am very happy to be working with all of you.”

The smile at the corners of his mouth was as warm as spring, and he said without any bureaucratic airs, “I had some last-minute business today and arrived late, delaying everyone’s lunch hour. I am truly sorry.”

“To ensure everyone doesn't go hungry, I won’t say much more. I hope that in the future, we can work together, do our jobs well, and live up to the expectations of our superiors.”

Without any long-winded speeches or grand declarations, Ji Zhengyao said a few casual words and looked at the secretary beside him.

Secretary Yao understood immediately and turned to Division Chief Huang, “Has a working lunch been arranged? Let’s eat together.”

Because they had been notified in advance, the cafeteria had indeed prepared a working lunch.

However, those were just for show; Division Chief Huang hadn't expected Ji Zhengyao to ask to eat with them.

But since Bureau Chief Ji had spoken, he couldn't object. He smiled and agreed enthusiastically, “Yes, yes, yes, then everyone, let’s go have the working lunch together.”

Obeying the leader’s arrangements was a required course for him.

Ling Ting: “...”

A big leader, why eat a working lunch?

“Sister Wang, can I not go?”

Ling Ting trailed at the very back of the line, asking Sister Wang in a tiny voice.

She was panicking and didn't want to go.

“How can you do that?”

There were four people in their office, and one was on leave; if Ling Ting didn't go, only she and Little Liu would be left, and they would be spotted immediately.

Division Chief Huang was acting very strangely today, and she didn't want to run into any trouble.

“Oh.”

Ling Ting’s escape attempt failed. She sighed with a mournful face and had no choice but to follow along slowly.

But precisely because she was slow, by the time she arrived at the cafeteria, all the seats were already full.

The food in their unit’s cafeteria was mediocre, and usually, there were only a few people eating there.

What was going on today?

Looking at the sea of heads, Ling Ting’s small face was full of shock.

“Little Ling, come, come, sit over here.”

Just as Ling Ting was holding her tray, standing there foolishly, not knowing where to go, Division Chief Huang’s voice came over.

“Chief, I won’t go over there.”

Seeing Division Chief Huang pointing to the seat next to Ji Zhengyao and calling her, Ling Ting was terrified and shook her head like a rattle.

“There are no seats left, just come over.”

Division Chief Huang didn't give her a chance to refuse at all. After saying that, he turned to talk to Bureau Chief Ji.

He was cunning and had long since realized that Ji Zhengyao knew Ling Ting.

This Bureau Chief Ji had an extraordinary background, and he needed to cultivate someone who could act as a messenger for him.

“Ling Ting, hurry up and go.”

Seeing Ling Ting standing there like a fool, Little Liu was afraid the leader would get angry, so she whispered to her.

Ling Ting had no choice but to walk over slowly.

“Sit here.”

Ji Zhengyao looked at Ling Ting, who had finally arrived after dawdling for a long time. A flicker of amusement crossed his eyes as he shifted to the side.

Ling Ting smiled awkwardly, said “Hello, Bureau Chief,” and braced herself to sit down.

Being stared at by all her colleagues, Ling Ting felt terrible, and her heart was beating nervously.

In all her years, other than the time in middle school when she didn't do her homework and had to stand by the podium for an entire morning, she had never been the center of such attention.

“Little Ling, is it?”

Seeing Ling Ting eating in small bites, her shoulders hunched in a timid, put-upon manner, Ji Zhengyao found it quite interesting.

Ling Ting was lost in her own thoughts. Hearing Ji Zhengyao’s words, she instantly tensed up, and a mouthful of rice got stuck in her throat. She coughed so hard that tears came to her eyes.

“Are you alright?”

Seeing Ling Ting’s face flush red from coughing, Ji Zhengyao reached out instinctively, but pulled his hand back halfway.

Ling Ting was startled by his gesture and coughed even harder.

“No... *cough, cough, cough*... I’m fine.”

“Drink some water.”

Ji Zhengyao also knew that his previous action had been a bit over the line, so he immediately looked at Secretary Yao...

chapters.title: An Awkward Lunch
chapters.content:
Secretary Yao, a sharp-witted person, immediately handed over the water glass from the table.

Ling Ting didn't think much of it; she took the glass and gulped down a few mouthfuls.

She had been choking to death.

"Little Ling, are you alright?"

Director Huang glanced at the glass in Ling Ting's hand, his eyes flickering, and he asked her in a gentle, amiable tone.

"I'm fine now, Director."

After drinking some water, Ling Ting finally felt less uncomfortable.

"If you're fine, then let's eat."

Ji Zhengyao's voice sounded again.

The young girl's face had been flushed from holding her breath; it was clear how uncomfortable she had been just a moment ago.

Because of the blind date, Ling Ting was incredibly embarrassed. She didn't dare look at Ji Zhengyao and kept her head down, eating voraciously, though it tasted like chewing wax.

Going on a blind date with Bureau Chief Ji—and being an impostor at that—was something only she could have managed.

She was sitting too close to Ji Zhengyao; their shoulders were touching, and they could both feel the warmth radiating from each other.

Ling Ting was very nervous, her body stiff, not daring to move an inch.

"Not to your taste?"

Sensing Ling Ting's restraint, Ji Zhengyao turned his head and asked in a low voice.

"No."

Blushing, she shook her head, dodging his warm, pleasant scent.

Feeling Ling Ting's resistance, Ji Zhengyao paused slightly, shifted his body away, and stopped bothering her.

Ling Ting ate this meal with her heart in her throat. As soon as she finished, she ran back to the office before the leaders had even left.

She had to run; she was dying of embarrassment.

In that short time, she had nearly clawed a three-bedroom apartment out of the floor with her toes.

Back in the office, Ling Ting let out a long, heavy breath. Like a thief, she pressed herself against the window to look toward the unit's entrance.

Ji Zhengyao seemed to have something to attend to and was leaving. Director Huang had already seen him out, and the two were shaking hands, though she couldn't tell what they were saying.

Looking at Ji Zhengyao's handsome profile, Ling Ting sighed once more at how well-matched he and her cousin were.

Suddenly, for some reason, Ji Zhengyao looked up. His eagle-like eyes locked onto her precisely, giving Ling Ting a fright.

She quickly pulled her head back and crouched down, not daring to peek again for a long time.

"Ling Ting, what are you doing?"

After seeing off the leaders, Sister Wang returned to the office and asked, puzzled to see Ling Ting crouching on the floor.

"Nothing, I dropped something."

Ling Ting pretended to look for something on the floor before standing up as if nothing had happened.

She leaned back and stood on her tiptoes to glance downstairs, and only when she saw that Ji Zhengyao's car was gone did she finally relax.

"Ling Ting, I saw you chatting and laughing with Bureau Chief Ji. Did you know each other before?"

Sister Wang hadn't been working at the unit for a year or two; she had a sharp eye.

Although Ling Ting was usually very shy and honest, her behavior today was clearly unusual.

"I don't know him. How could I possibly know such a big shot?"

Ling Ting kept her head down, rummaging through her desk as if to cover her tracks.

She was truly afraid that her colleagues would find out about her blind date with Ji Zhengyao.

If rumors started flying, it would be a disaster.

"That's true. How could we little people know Bureau Chief Ji?"

"It was probably just Director Huang pushing Ling Ting forward to liven up the atmosphere."

Little Liu walked in and chimed in with a smile, helping Ling Ting out of the spot.

"That's true, too."

Hearing Little Liu's words, Sister Wang put away the suspicion on her face and didn't press further.

"Phew."

With Sister Wang no longer digging for answers, Ling Ting relaxed completely and plopped into her chair.

She had spent the day on pins and needles; she could finally rest for a while.

But just as she let her guard down, Secretary Xiao Gao, who worked for Director Huang, arrived.

"Ling Ting, the Director wants you to come over for a moment."

"Me?"

Since Ling Ting started working here, Director Huang had never proactively sought her out. What was going on these past two days?

"Ling Ting, hurry up and go."

Seeing Ling Ting dazed again, Little Liu reminded her.

"Oh."

Ling Ting stood up blankly and followed Secretary Xiao Gao.

"This Ling Ting, what is going on with her today?"

Sister Wang stared at Ling Ting's retreating back, muttering to herself.

Little Liu didn't look up; while fiddling with his camera, he said distractedly, "Maybe she's tired from preparing for her wedding."

Thinking of Ling Ting getting married soon, a flash of disappointment crossed Little Liu's eyes.

"So young, I don't know what the rush is."

Thinking about having to shell out money for a wedding gift, Sister Wang forgot about the gossip and huffed, heading off for her nap.

Ling Ting had no idea that Sister Wang was lamenting the money she was about to spend on a gift; she was feeling anxious and uneasy.

Why did the Director call her over?

She hadn't done anything wrong, had she?

"Little Ling, come, come."

Seeing Ling Ting arrive, Director Huang was much more enthusiastic than usual, even personally pouring her a glass of water.

Ling Ting was flattered, feeling as if the glass in her hand weighed a thousand pounds.

"Sit, sit, sit."

Director Huang smiled amiably, his wrinkled face blooming like a chrysanthemum.

"Director, you called me here—is there something you need me to do?"

Ling Ting couldn't handle the Director's sudden warmth; she set down the glass and asked cautiously.

"Actually, it's nothing much."

Director Huang sat back behind his desk, rubbing his hands together, smiling. "Ling Ting, why did Bureau Chief Ji call you 'Lin' today?"

Although Bureau Chief Ji had only spoken two sentences to Ling Ting, Director Huang had caught a glimpse of many unusual things.

"Director, I don't know either."

How could Ling Ting dare to say she had been on a blind date with Bureau Chief Ji?

If that got out, she would become a local celebrity at the office.

Besides, it wouldn't be good for Bureau Chief Ji either.

"He must have mistaken me for someone else."

Ling Ting found a random excuse.

"Is that so?"

Director Huang clearly didn't believe her.

"Director, I really don't know Bureau Chief Ji."

Ling Ting pouted, picking at her fingers, nearly on the verge of tears.

"Alright, alright, alright. If you don't know him, then forget it."

The few hairs on Director Huang's head had been lost to playing mind games; seeing Ling Ting's eyes turn red, he didn't press further.

After all, he wasn't sure about the relationship between Bureau Chief Ji and Ling Ting, and he couldn't push too hard.

In any case, there was plenty of time; he would find out the truth sooner or later.

Ling Ting had assumed the Director would dig to the bottom of it and wouldn't stop until he got what he wanted.

To her surprise, he let her go after just two questions.

Walking out of Director Huang's office, she still felt a bit dizzy.

That was it?

...

Because of the tension, Ling Ting was restless for the entire afternoon.

She finally managed to make it to the end of the workday, packed up, and without even saying goodbye to her colleagues, she slipped away.

"Ling Ting."

Just as she reached the unit's main gate, she was blocked by Qin Nan.

"What are you doing here?"

Ling Ting asked, her expression indifferent.

"Ling Ting, can you stop this, please?"

Qin Nan's face still looked sour, but his tone had softened significantly.

"Qin Nan, I've already made it very clear to you; there's really no need to keep pestering me."

Although Ling Ting had a soft personality, once she made a decision, she wouldn't change it.

With Qin Nan, she couldn't see a future.

"Ling Ting, we've been together for two years. Are you really willing to break up?"

Qin Nan had always been confident, believing Ling Ting was just angry for a moment and wouldn't truly break up with him.

If he played the emotional card, she would change her mind.

"Qin Nan, I'm serious."

Ling Ting looked at Qin Nan, her eyes filled with a firmness he had never seen before.

"What I want is a warm, small home, not someone who calculates and schemes before we're even married."

chapters.title: A Breakup Gift
chapters.content:
Thinking of the grievances she had suffered while with Qin Nan over the past two years, Ling Ting’s voice choked up slightly. "Qin Nan, we can't go back to how things were."

After saying this, she turned and walked away.

"Ling Ting?"

Qin Nan tried to grab Ling Ting’s hand, but she shook him off forcefully.

Watching Ling Ting’s resolute back, a part of Qin Nan’s heart suddenly felt empty.

He felt that Ling Ting might really not want to be with him anymore.

Because of Qin Nan’s pestering, Ling Ting temporarily forgot the embarrassment Ji Zhengyao had caused her.

Back home, she lay on the sofa for a long time until her stomach let out a grumbling protest, prompting her to get up and cook.

She hadn't eaten well while sitting next to Ji Zhengyao at noon.

Thinking of Ji Zhengyao, Ling Ting shook her head and sighed helplessly.

Although that man always wore a smile and seemed to have a good temper, his presence was too overwhelming, and Ling Ting was afraid of him.

She cooked a simple bowl of noodles and watched a show while eating, but she ended up crying as she watched.

She couldn't even figure out exactly why she was crying.

"Ding-ling."

Just as Ling Ting was sobbing uncontrollably, unable to even eat her meal, her phone rang.

She put down her chopsticks, picked up her phone, and glanced at it, nearly screaming in fright.

It was Ji Zhengyao!

Don't ask why Ling Ting knew it was him; his WeChat display name was his real name.

[What are you doing?]

Looking at those three words on the screen, Ling Ting was momentarily at a loss.

Why would a dignified bureau chief be messaging her?

Ling Ting was full of confusion.

If it were an ordinary superior, out of respect, she would have replied even after work.

But they had been on a blind date, and she was an impostor—just thinking about it made her feel awkward.

She stared at her phone for so long that she eventually drifted off to sleep, still not having figured out how to reply to Ji Zhengyao.

When she woke up the next morning, she "accidentally" deleted the message on purpose.

...

"We have field work this afternoon, you guys..."

Xiao Liu fiddled with the camera in his hand, paused, and glanced at Sister Wang.

Because of the arrival of the new bureau chief, the usually slack Section Chief Huang was acting like he’d been injected with adrenaline. He had held a special meeting that morning and assigned a lot of work.

Although their department’s work was a bit miscellaneous, they were primarily responsible for the official website and new media.

New broom sweeps clean; before Bureau Chief Ji could even start, the Section Chief had already lit the fire himself.

He said that from now on, the website had to post one update every day, and each post had to include clear, meaningful photos.

Anything that hadn't received enough likes in the past had to be deleted and redone.

Xiao Liu, being a man, didn't mind field work; in fact, he was quite willing to go out.

But...

"I still have some things to handle, Ling Ting, you go."

Sister Wang didn't even look up, directing Ling Ting, who was organizing documents, in a righteous tone.

Ling Ting’s hand paused. She looked at Xiao Liu helplessly and nodded in agreement.

She knew this task would eventually fall on her.

"Ling Ting, actually, if you didn't go, she couldn't really say anything."

While they were heading downstairs, Xiao Liu, who usually didn't talk much, suddenly spoke up.

With Xiao Lu on leave, Ling Ting had been doing all the recent field work; it should have been Sister Wang’s turn.

"Forget it, field work is actually quite nice."

Ling Ting smiled, not wanting to make a fuss.

Sister Wang relied on her seniority to frequently boss the newcomers around.

If it were just her, it would be fine, but if you refused, you’d have to endure her cold shoulder for days.

Xiao Lu, who shared the office, had argued with her more than once.

However, Ling Ting wasn't good at arguing, so she never refused.

"You really have a good temper."

Xiao Liu smiled and didn't ask any more, walking to the car to open the door for Ling Ting.

The two got along well and worked efficiently, finishing their tasks and leaving work by four o'clock in the afternoon.

Back home, Ling Ting opened the fridge and was just about to make something to eat when her phone rang.

It was a call from her good friend, Qiao Yin.

"Ling Ting, I'm back! Are you free to grab a bite to eat?"

Qiao Yin was Ling Ting’s college classmate; they had slept in bunk beds for four years.

After graduation, she opened a small online shop, selling personalized clothing she designed herself.

Because her work was flexible, traveling became a part of her life.

She had just returned from Thailand and was calling her immediately.

"Sure, how about tomorrow night?"

Ling Ting hadn't seen Qiao Yin in a month and missed her.

"Okay, let's meet at our usual spot. Bye."

After expressing her intent, Qiao Yin hung up without hesitation.

Ling Ting listened to the dial tone, shook her head, and continued puttering around in the kitchen.

Although she cooked every day, it was always just simple noodles or fried rice; she wasn't very good at complex dishes.

After making a vegetable soup and serving half a bowl of rice, she turned on her computer.

She had a habit: she had to watch a show while eating.

Even though she was too restless to really pay attention, listening to the voices from the show made her feel less lonely.

Living alone, she always wanted some background noise.

"Ding-ling."

Just as she put a mouthful of rice into her mouth, her phone chimed.

[What are you doing?]

Ji Zhengyao again?

Ling Ting put down her chopsticks, her pretty little face instantly scrunching up.

She hadn't replied, so why was he still messaging?

[Get some rest early.]

Just as Ling Ting was struggling with whether or not to reply to Ji Zhengyao, he sent another message.

Looking at those four words on the screen, Ling Ting felt a sense of relief, and her heart finally settled.

But just as she relaxed, Ling Ting seemed to think of something, and her eyes widened instantly.

Her aunt said the other side agreed to give it a try—Ji Zhengyao couldn't be serious, could he?

Oh god, how was she going to end this?

Because she kept worrying about this, Ling Ting lost her appetite and went to bed early.

The next day, Ling Ting followed Xiao Liu around for the whole morning again. After getting off work, she headed to the place she had agreed to meet Qiao Yin.

The two often ate at a buffet restaurant; it was reasonably priced, had a wide variety of food, and most importantly, it wasn't far from either of them.

"Qiao Yin, how did you get so tan?"

Ling Ting asked, full of surprise, when she saw the tanned Qiao Yin.

Qiao Yin wore her hair in a neat short cut, and her originally fair cheeks were more than a few shades darker.

"Oh, I didn't use sunscreen, so I ended up like this."

Qiao Yin didn't care, shrugged, and grabbed Ling Ting’s hand to go get some good food.

Don't look at how thin they both were—together they didn't even weigh two hundred pounds—but when it came to eating at a buffet, they were formidable.

After getting their first round of food, they went to a quiet corner and started chatting while they ate.

"Ling Ting, you have no idea how much fun I had this past month."

Qiao Yin put a peeled shrimp into Ling Ting’s bowl and said with glowing eyes, "I went to Thailand first, then Myanmar. Anyway, I went everywhere I could."

"I even saw ladyboys!"

Qiao Yin was beaming, as if she had gained some massive advantage.

"Really? Did you touch them?"

Ling Ting smiled and followed up on Qiao Yin’s comment.

Back in school, Qiao Yin was always the bold one, often secretly eyeing handsome guys.

Although Ling Ting was more reserved, there were no taboos between them; they said whatever they wanted.

"Of course!"

Qiao Yin leaned in close to Ling Ting with a mischievous look, raising an eyebrow. "The feel was explosive."

"Hehe."

Ling Ting loved listening to Qiao Yin; she was always so cheerful and lively.

Unlike herself, who had no great talents and couldn't speak her mind.

"Are you going away again anytime soon?"

Ling Ting looked at Qiao Yin, smiling as she helped her pick up some food.

"No, I'm tired. We'll see next year."

chapters.title: Trouble at the Door
chapters.content:
Her savings were mostly spent; she didn't have the money to leave even if she wanted to.

"That’s wonderful! We can be together again from now on."

Ling Ting didn't know about Qiao Yin's situation, and her eyes curved into crescents with a smile.

"Oh, by the way, Ling Ting, I even bought you a wedding gift."

Qiao Yin seemed to remember something; she slapped her forehead, opened her bag, and took out a small red velvet box.

Ling Ting’s expression changed at Qiao Yin’s words, and she pulled at the corner of her mouth awkwardly. "Qiao Yin, Qin Nan and I have broken up."

"What?"

Qiao Yin held the velvet box, her face full of astonishment.

"Broken up? Why?"

In Qiao Yin’s impression, Ling Ting and Qin Nan had never even argued, had they?

Well...

Ling Ting had a good temper; even if there were disagreements, she was the one who always compromised.

Seeing Qiao Yin’s confusion, Ling Ting didn't hide anything and told her everything that had happened during this time.

"Qin Nan’s family is too much!"

Qiao Yin slammed the box in her hand onto the table, furious.

"Knowing your situation, they still wanted you to pay for the renovations? And what’s even more infuriating is that they wanted you to sign some prenuptial agreement. Isn't that clearly bullying you?"

Ling Ting had no parents and had only been working for a short time. Even if others didn't know, Qin Nan should have been well aware of it.

"It’s alright, it’s all in the past. We’ve already broken up."

Although she still felt sad when she thought of Qin Nan, Ling Ting had already come to terms with a lot of it.

"When I run into Qin Nan, I’m definitely going to give him a piece of my mind."

Qiao Yin let out a "hmph" and took Ling Ting’s hand, feeling sorry for her.

"Since you aren't getting married anymore, just take this gift as a breakup present."

Qiao Yin didn't dwell on it and shoved the gift into Ling Ting’s hand.

"What is it?"

Ling Ting looked at the box in her hand, her eyes reddening, and she asked Qiao Yin in a muffled voice.

"It’s a bracelet."

Qiao Yin sensed the shift in Ling Ting’s emotions, took the gift out, and put it on her wrist.

The bracelet was something she had specifically saved up to buy—green agate interspersed with three small gold beads; it suited Ling Ting perfectly.

"A breakup is a breakup. There are plenty of good men out there."

Qiao Yin patted Ling Ting’s hand, offering gentle comfort.

"Thank you."

Looking at the gift Qiao Yin had carefully prepared for her, Ling Ting was deeply moved.

Although she only had this one good friend in her four years of college, one was worth ten.

Qiao Yin was a ray of sunshine; seeing that Ling Ting was in a bad mood, she kept telling jokes to cheer her up.

Afraid that she would get sick from bottling things up alone, she even made plans for them to go to an amusement park on the weekend.

Qin Nan was stingy with money, so Ling Ting hadn't been to an amusement park in a long time. She hesitated for a moment before agreeing.

She was spending her own money; no one had the right to say anything.

After the two of them finished their meal happily, they went to the subway station and headed home.

But just as she arrived at the entrance of her apartment complex, she was stopped by a somewhat familiar voice.

"Ling Ting!"

Ling Ting froze for a second and slowly turned around.

"Di... Director Ji?"

Ling Ting appeared somewhat uneasy, and her small face flushed red.

Seeing Ji Zhengyao made her nervous and guilty.

"Where have you been so late?"

Ji Zhengyao stepped out of his car and walked calmly toward Ling Ting, his handsome face devoid of his professional smile.

He was wearing a white shirt with the sleeves rolled up to his elbows, and there was a faint scent of tobacco on him.

"I went out to eat with a friend."

Ji Zhengyao was tall with a powerful presence. Standing face-to-face with him, Ling Ting instantly felt a sense of oppression and subconsciously took a step back.

Sensing her resistance, Ji Zhengyao frowned imperceptibly and took a step forward.

"It’s too late for a girl to be out alone. I’ll take you back."

Ji Zhengyao pointed to his car.

Domineering and forceful.

"Director Ji, I’m already here."

At this moment, Ling Ting was very grateful that she had run into Ji Zhengyao at the entrance of her home.

Ji Zhengyao: "..."

"You live here?"

Glancing at the complex behind Ling Ting, Ji Zhengyao’s expression darkened.

The complex didn't even have a security guard; the safety factor was far too low.

"Director Ji, it’s too late, so I won't invite you up."

Ling Ting smiled shyly and said with a hint of secret delight, "I’m going back to sleep now."

"...Hmm."

Ji Zhengyao nodded.

He watched as Ling Ting ran into the complex.

...

Ji Zhengyao felt stifled.

Because he felt frustrated, Ji Zhengyao, who had intended to go home, changed direction and headed straight for a club in the city center.

"Oh, Director Ji, you’re quite free, aren't you?"

Li Sheng handed a glass of wine to Ji Zhengyao, a mocking smile on his face.

Ji Zhengyao was a very busy man; he was usually so occupied he barely had time to stand still, and he hadn't come out to eat with him in a long time.

Ji Zhengyao took the glass, took a small sip, and said nothing.

"What, work stress?"

The two were high school classmates and had served in the military together; they had known each other for many years.

Seeing Ji Zhengyao looking so preoccupied, he assumed it was some trouble with his new appointment.

"Li Sheng, do you think it’s possible to forget someone after ten years?"

"What do you mean?"

Li Sheng sat down next to Ji Zhengyao and reached out to turn off the music.

"Nothing."

Ji Zhengyao swirled the wine in his glass, suddenly not wanting to talk about it.

"Old Ji, leaving things half-said is just teasing me, isn't it?"

Li Sheng was so frustrated he was practically tearing his hair out, his rugged, chiseled face full of curiosity.

Seeing that he had piqued Li Sheng's interest but was acting like nothing was wrong, Ji Zhengyao snatched the glass out of his hand.

"Say what you have to say."

Ji Zhengyao shook his head, his mouth as if sealed shut.

Ten years. That little girl no longer recognized him.

"You really are something."

Li Sheng understood Ji Zhengyao; despite the constant smile on his face, he was actually very deep. If he didn't want to talk about something, you couldn't get it out of him.

"Fine, come find me when you want to talk."

Li Sheng returned the glass to Ji Zhengyao and clinked his own against it in resignation.

The two had a couple of drinks before Ji Zhengyao made an excuse and left. After returning home, he stood by the window, unable to sleep all night.

He had always had trouble sleeping, getting at most three or four hours a night.

Ten years had passed, and despite taking plenty of medication, there had been no improvement.

The heatwave continued. Ling Ting had been out in the field for three days straight, her skin sunburned red, and she finally made it to the weekend.

Because she was so exhausted, she slept until noon. If her aunt hadn't called on video, who knows how long she would have stayed buried in bed.

Her aunt seemed very happy these past two days; not only did she not complain about her cousin, but she also said she had joined a tour group and was leaving for a trip the day after tomorrow.

After her parents passed away, her aunt was her closest relative. Hearing that she was going on a trip, Ling Ting worriedly gave her a long list of instructions.

However, her aunt complained that she was nagging and hung up the phone like a rebellious child.

Ling Ting looked at the phone in her hand, shook her head with a smile, and got up to go to the kitchen to cook.

It was too hot, so she decided on soybean paste noodles for today.

After finishing lunch, she intended to do some laundry and tidy up the room, but before she could start, there was a knock at the door.

After opening it, she discovered that the person outside was none other than Qin Nan’s mother.

"Auntie, why are you here?"

Ling Ting was very surprised by the arrival of Qin Nan’s mother.

Of course, she wasn't exactly welcoming either.

"Your place is really hard to find."

Qin Nan’s mother pursed her lips, her eyes filled with reproach.

Ling Ting, who had originally intended to invite her in, suddenly lost the desire to do so.

"I’ve already broken up with Qin Nan. Is there something you need?"

Qin Nan’s mother’s face fell instantly.

"Ling Ting, what kind of talk is that?"

"Auntie, I’m telling the truth."

Ling Ting lowered her eyes, feeling a sense of irritation, and retorted firmly...

chapters.title: Circuitous Tactics
chapters.content:
Qin Nan’s mother had high cheekbones and small eyes. She always held her chin up when she spoke, wearing an overbearing expression.

She was truly detestable.

“Ling Ting, I used to think you were quite nice. Why are you so impolite now?”

Qin Nan’s mother pushed Ling Ting aside and sashayed into the room, her hips swaying.

She scanned the room, even glancing into the bedroom, before finally sitting down on the small sofa in the living room.

“Ling Ting, it’s not that I want to lecture you, but you’ve been with Qin Nan for two years now. How can you just say you want to break up?”

In her mind, Ling Ting had no one to rely on, so even if they were having a spat, it was just her being temperamental.

There was no need to pay her any mind.

However, her son was clearly taking it seriously. Her feigned illness hadn’t worked; he hadn’t eaten all day yesterday, and he had even taken time off work in the afternoon.

He was the only precious gem in their family, and she truly couldn’t bear to see him sad.

Ling Ting’s attempt to establish boundaries before marriage had made her furious. She had come today to settle the score.

She was going to teach Ling Ting a lesson so that she wouldn’t dare to make things difficult for Qin Nan in the future.

“Auntie, there is no future for Qin Nan and me.”

Ling Ting stood before Qin Nan’s mother, staring stubbornly at a cup on the coffee table, once again expressing that she would not reconcile with Qin Nan.

This woman was disrespectful of her age and spent all day plotting against her. Ling Ting rarely hated anyone, but Qin Nan’s mother was an exception.

“Are you causing this trouble with Qin Nan because of the prenuptial agreement?”

Qin Nan’s mother was dissatisfied with Ling Ting’s attitude and spoke in a sarcastic tone. “Ling Ting, it’s not that I want to lecture you, but isn’t it a bit much to break up over such a small matter?”

Ling Ting didn’t speak, and Qin Nan’s mother continued, “Marriage isn’t a way to get rich. Why aren’t you learning to be better at such a young age?”

Qin Nan’s mother felt that since she was an elder, Ling Ting wouldn’t dare say anything even if she spoke like this.

After all, she had said much harsher things than this in the past.

“Auntie, what do you mean by ‘getting rich through marriage’? Aside from the down payment of a hundred thousand or so for the house, has your family ever spent a single cent on me?”

Ling Ting’s face flushed red with anger. If she hadn’t been trying hard to control herself, tears would have already fallen.

“Is a down payment of over a hundred thousand not money?”

Qin Nan’s mother slapped the coffee table and snorted coldly. “Your appetite is truly huge.”

“Please leave!”

Ling Ting was trembling with rage. She rushed over and pushed the door open.

Pointing outside, she issued an eviction order in a shaking voice, “My appetite is too big for your family to satisfy, so don’t come here again.”
